newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Twenty drown in Nigerian boat disaster.
newsitem.headline: Twenty drown in Nigerian boat disaster.

text.p: About 20 people drowned when their boat capsized in the Qua Iboe river off the southeastern Nigerian state of Akwa Ibom, an official of an oil company that took part in the rescue operations said on Thursday.
He said the victims, whose bodies were washed ashore, were believed to be traders heading for neighbouring Cameroon.
Local newspapers put the death toll at between 100 and 150 in the accident which occurred last weekend but the oil company official said the figure was vastly exaggerated.
"That is an overblown figure," he said. "The rescue team saved the lives of 36 people. Though the boat was overloaded, I don't think it had a capacity for even 100 people.
"The number of those who drowned couldn't have been more than 20," he added.
He said the cause of the accident was not clear.
Boat accidents are common along Nigeria's Atlantic coastline where many of the vessels have no on-board radios to call for help in emergencies.
